 Duke guard Nikolas Khamenia (14) and UConn guard Silas Demary Jr. (2) battle for the ball as UConn guard Braylon Mullins looks away during the first half in the Elite Eight of the NCAA college basketball tournament, Sunday, March 29, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)
 By Staff report | Hartford Courant Staff PUBLISHED: October 29, 2026 at 3:35 PM EDT | UPDATED: October 29, 2026 at 3:40 PM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... UConn men’s basketball stars Silas Demary Jr. and Braylon Mullins each earned a spot on the National Association of Basketball Coaches ‘ preseason watch list for national player of the year.
 The award, which will be determined by a nationwide vote of Division I head coaches at the end of the regular season, will be announced the week of the 2027 Final Four.
 Demary Jr. and Mullins are among 20 players nationally to earn a spot on the preseason list. UConn is one of three teams – along with Duke and Florida – to have multiple players on the list.
 The Big East Preseason Player of the Year, Demary Jr. enters his second season at UConn with a slew of preseason honors, including Preseason All-America nods from CBS Sports, Sports Illustrated, The Athletic and Field of 68. In his first year in Storrs last season, the 6-4 point guard averaged 10.1 points, 4.5 rebounds and a Big East-best 5.9 assists per game.
 Mullins was a Preseason First Team All-Big East pick and was named a First Team All-American by Blue Ribbon Report. Last season, he was a unanimous All-Freshman pick in the BIG East. The 6’6 Indiana native made 29 starts as a rookie and averaged 12.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game. He knocked down 72 threes, second-most in a season for a freshman in UConn history, including the iconic buzzer beater to send Due home in the Elite Eight.
 The NABC Division I Player of the Year award has been presented every season since 1974-75, and is the only national player of the year honor selected by the sport’s head coaches.
 Hines named to Karl Malone Watch List
 Sophomore Na’jai Hines was named to the Karl Malone Power Forward of the Year preseason watch list, the Naismith Hall of Fame announced Thursday. He’s among 20 players named to the preseason list.
 Entering his first season in Storrs, the big man averaged 6.5 points and 5.5 rebounds as a freshman a year ago at Seton Hall along with a BIG East-leading 2.2 blocks per game.
 Hines joins teammates Silas Demary Jr., a member of the Cousy Award Preseason List, Braylon Mullins on the West Award List and Colben Landrew on The Erving Award list as Huskies lauded by the Hall of Fame for positional awards thus far.
